text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000183 bills 99215 far above its risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity tier, including many low-complexity visits, but records are too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. The excess 99215 share holds at every complexity tier, not only among sicker patients. A third of 99215s went to patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as low back pain (C0107609, C0107790), rash (C0107357) and follow-up encounters (C0107257, C0107751). By contrast, the high-complexity 99215 samples (e.g., C0107425, C0108075) look clinically plausible. The documentation cannot settle the question: only 3 documented 99215 claims came back, 1 below the billed level (C0108094) and 2 supported (C0108190, C0108324). That is too few to judge. The 99214 results are only modestly above peers, and the 7 notes claiming moderate-plus data review without a lab line are weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition back-pain and follow-up visits, to see whether high-level MDM or time is genuinely documented."}
